units.source_text: 古歌：“秋草名藤袴，抛残在野郊。

en.t: An old poem says: Among autumn grasses is one called fujibakama, cast aside and left in the fields.

units.source_text: 不知谁脱下，只觉异香飘。”

en.t: Who took it off and left it there, I do not know; I only sense a strange fragrance drifting by.
This appears in the Kokin Wakashu.

units.source_text: 日文中的“藤袴”即中文兰草之意。

en.t: The Japanese word fujibakama means what Chinese calls orchid grass.
In Japanese, hakama refers to a skirt-like garment, not trousers.
